distr::Rayleigh object¶

The object form of the Rayleigh family: it carries the parameters, and offers the density, the distribution function, random draws, the cumulant generating function and the cumulants as methods, and a maximum-likelihood fit with standard errors.

Signature¶

distr::Rayleigh(double sigma);
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::pdf(const pluss::Series& x) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::logpdf(const pluss::Series& x) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::cdf(const pluss::Series& x) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::logcdf(const pluss::Series& x) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::sample(std::initializer_list<std::int64_t> sizes, pluss::Config cfg = {}, std::uint64_t seed = 0) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::sample_like(const pluss::Series& like, std::uint64_t seed = 0) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::cgf(const pluss::Series& t) const;
pluss::Series distr::Rayleigh::cumulant(std::int64_t order) const;
distr::RayleighFit distr::Rayleigh::MLE(const pluss::Series& x) const;

What It Does¶

distr::Rayleigh holds the parameters of the Rayleigh distribution, so that they are written once and the same object is used for every evaluation. Its methods give the same numbers as the kind-based functions distr::pdf(dst::Rayleigh, ...) and the others, on a whole Series at once.

  • pdf, logpdf, cdf and logcdf evaluate the density, the distribution function and their logarithms.

  • sample draws a Series of the given shape; sample_like draws one with the shape and dtype of an existing Series. The seed fixes the stream.

  • cgf(t) is the cumulant generating function log E[exp(t X)], and cumulant(order) the cumulant of that order (the first is the mean, the second the variance).

  • MLE(x) fits the family to observed values by maximum likelihood and returns a RayleighFit with the estimates (fields sigma), their standard errors, 95% intervals and the log-likelihood.

The parameters of the family are described on the Rayleigh page.

Parameters¶

double sigma

sigma is the scale parameter.

const pluss::Series& x

The points at which to evaluate, a Series of any shape; the result has the same shape.

std::initializer_list<std::int64_t> sizes

The shape of the array of random draws, for example {n} or {rows, columns}.

pluss::Config cfg

The dtype and platform of the draws; the default is Float32 on the CPU, so request Float64 when precision matters.

std::uint64_t seed

The seed of the stream. The same seed always gives the same draws; a seed of 0 is a fixed default, not a random one.

const pluss::Series& like

A Series whose shape and dtype sample_like copies for the draws; its values are not used.

const pluss::Series& t

The points at which to evaluate the cumulant generating function.

std::int64_t order

The order of the cumulant: 1 is the mean, 2 the variance, 3 the third cumulant, and so on.

const pluss::Series& x (for MLE)

The observed values to fit, one-dimensional and inside the support of the family.

Returns¶

pdf, logpdf, cdf, logcdf and cgf return a Series of the shape of their argument; sample and sample_like return the drawn Series; cumulant returns a one-element Series. MLE returns a RayleighFit.

Errors¶

  • Parameters outside their valid range are refused when a method is called (scale must be positive).

Methods¶

  • pdf – the density (mass function) at each point.

  • logpdf – the logarithm of the density.

  • cdf – the distribution function.

  • logcdf – the logarithm of the distribution function.

  • sample – random draws of a given shape.

  • sample_like – random draws with the shape and dtype of an existing Series.

  • cgf – the cumulant generating function.

  • cumulant – the cumulant of a given order.

  • MLE – the maximum-likelihood fit with standard errors and intervals.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

Example 1 uses the object form, distr::Rayleigh, which carries the parameters and offers the same functions as methods, plus cumulant for the moments.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace distr = pluss::subsp::stats::distr;
namespace dst = distr::dst;

int main() {
  const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(5);

  const distr::Rayleigh d{1.5};
  const auto sample = d.sample({200000}, f64, 11ULL);
  const auto at = pluss::make_series({2.5}, f64);

  std::cout << "pdf at 2.5: " << as_f64(d.pdf(at)) << '\n';
  std::cout << "cdf at 2.5: " << as_f64(d.cdf(at)) << '\n';
  const double m = as_f64(sample.mean());
  const double v = as_f64(((sample - m) * (sample - m)).mean());
  std::cout << "cumulant(1), the mean: " << as_f64(d.cumulant(1)) << "   mean of 200000 draws: " << m << '\n';
  std::cout << "cumulant(2), the variance: " << as_f64(d.cumulant(2)) << "   variance of the draws: " << v << '\n';
}

Output

pdf at 2.5: 0.27706
cdf at 2.5: 0.75065
cumulant(1), the mean: 1.87997   mean of 200000 draws: 1.88288
cumulant(2), the variance: 0.96571   variance of the draws: 0.96617

cumulant(1) and cumulant(2) are the exact mean (1.87997) and variance (0.96571) of the distribution, computed from the parameters without drawing anything; the mean (1.88288) and variance (0.96617) of 200000 draws land within sampling error of them (the standard error of the mean is about 0.0022).

Example 2¶

Example 2 uses every evaluation method of the object distr::Rayleigh: the density (mass function), its logarithm, the distribution function and its logarithm, the cumulant generating function cgf, and the cumulants of orders 1 to 4.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace distr = pluss::subsp::stats::distr;
namespace dst = distr::dst;

int main() {
  const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(5);

  const distr::Rayleigh d{1.5};
  const auto x = pluss::make_series({0.25, 0.75, 1.5, 2.5}, f64);
  const auto t = pluss::make_series({0.1, 0.2, 0.3}, f64);

  std::cout << "x:";
  for (double v : x.pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "pdf:";
  for (double v : d.pdf(x).pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "logpdf:";
  for (double v : d.logpdf(x).pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "cdf:";
  for (double v : d.cdf(x).pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "logcdf:";
  for (double v : d.logcdf(x).pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "cgf at t = 0.1 0.2 0.3:";
  for (double v : d.cgf(t).pull<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';

  std::cout << "cumulants 1 to 4:";
  for (int order = 1; order <= 4; ++order) std::cout << ' ' << as_f64(d.cumulant(order));
  std::cout << '\n';
}

Output

x: 0.25000 0.75000 1.50000 2.50000
pdf: 0.10958 0.29417 0.40435 0.27706
logpdf: -2.21111 -1.22361 -0.90547 -1.28353
cdf: 0.01379 0.11750 0.39347 0.75065
logcdf: -4.28360 -2.14129 -0.93275 -0.28682
cgf at t = 0.1 0.2 0.3: 0.19293 0.39612 0.61021
cumulants 1 to 4: 1.87997 0.96571 0.59893 0.22857

logpdf and logcdf are the logarithms of the density and of the distribution function, computed directly, which is more accurate in the tails than taking the logarithm of a tiny number: at the first point exp(-2.21111) = 0.10958, the density 0.10958 printed above. The cumulants are 1.87997, 0.96571, 0.59893, 0.22857: the first is the mean, the second the variance, the third measures skewness (it is zero for a symmetric distribution), and the fourth the excess of the tails over a normal one. The cumulants are the Taylor coefficients of cgf: 0.1 κ1 + 0.1² κ2 / 2 + 0.1³ κ3 / 6 + 0.1⁴ κ4 / 24 = 0.19293 against cgf(0.1) = 0.19293.

Example 3¶

Example 3 draws random values from the object: sample_like takes the shape and dtype of an existing Series, sample takes a shape, and the seed fixes the stream; a large sample reproduces the first two cumulants.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace distr = pluss::subsp::stats::distr;
namespace dst = distr::dst;

int main() {
  const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(5);

  const distr::Rayleigh d{1.5};

  // sample_like draws a Series with the shape and dtype of an existing one; the seed fixes the stream.
  const auto like = pluss::series::zeros({2, 3}, f64);
  const auto draws = d.sample_like(like, 11ULL);
  std::cout << "shape of the draws: " << draws.sizes()[0] << " x " << draws.sizes()[1] << "\n";

  const auto again = d.sample_like(like, 11ULL);
  std::cout << "same seed, same draws: " << (as_f64((draws - again).abs().max()) == 0.0 ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";
  const auto other = d.sample_like(like, 12ULL);
  std::cout << "other seed, other draws: " << (as_f64((draws - other).abs().max()) > 0.0 ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";

  // sample takes the shape directly; a large sample estimates the mean and the variance.
  const auto big = d.sample({200000}, f64, 5ULL);
  const double m = as_f64(big.mean());
  const double v = as_f64(((big - m) * (big - m)).mean());
  std::cout << "mean of 200000 draws " << m << " (cumulant(1) = " << as_f64(d.cumulant(1)) << ")\n";
  std::cout << "variance of 200000 draws " << v << " (cumulant(2) = " << as_f64(d.cumulant(2)) << ")\n";
}

Output

shape of the draws: 2 x 3
same seed, same draws: yes
other seed, other draws: yes
mean of 200000 draws 1.87786 (cumulant(1) = 1.87997)
variance of 200000 draws 0.97111 (cumulant(2) = 0.96571)

Example 4¶

Example 4 fits the family back to 1000 draws by maximum likelihood with MLE, and reads the estimates, their standard errors, the 95% intervals and the log-likelihood.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace distr = pluss::subsp::stats::distr;
namespace dst = distr::dst;

int main() {
  const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);

  const auto x = distr::Rayleigh{1.5}.sample({1000}, f64, 20261022ULL);
  const auto fit = distr::Rayleigh{}.MLE(x);

  std::cout << "sigma: " << fit.sigma << '\n';
  std::cout << "stderr:";
  for (double v : fit.stderr(x).host<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "95% bounds:";
  for (double v : fit.confint(x).host<double>()) std::cout << ' ' << v;
  std::cout << '\n';
  std::cout << "loglik: " << as_f64(fit.loglik(x)) << '\n';
}

Output

sigma: 1.5028
stderr: 0.0238
95% bounds: 1.4562 1.5493
loglik: -1331.3522

The fit recovers the generating values: sigma 1.5028 against a true 1.5 (0.12 standard errors away). The 95% bounds are the estimate ± 1.96 standard errors, one pair per parameter in the order of the fit’s fields, and the log-likelihood is the quantity to compare against other families fitted to the same data.
